name: Deep Vinaceous-Lavender
lede: Deep Vinaceous-Lavender is a dusty, wine-tinted lavender, Ridgway's reading of a muted purplish grey.

sections.title: Wine and lavender together
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 nomenclature gives the swatch as plate XLIV, hue 65′′′, tone d, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 reads it as a pale reddish purple, about 3.1 units from the block center [1]. "Vinaceous" is the library's wine-toned branch of the purple family, paired here with [[lavender]] rather than left alone [1].

The nearest named color in our data is [[heliotrope-grey]], about 3.7 units off, which our library also names as its closest match; [[deep-greyish-lavender]] and [[purplish-lilac]] sit a little further out [1][2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This color, as photographed, appears in 58 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.24 percent, rarer than 57 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 8 of 1,674 paintings, at 0.5 percent of that period's paintings, 2.5 times the overall rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light [3]. It is most over-represented in France (2.6 times expected; 16 of 3443 paintings) [3]. The earliest match in the archive is a 1452 painting by Bartolomeo Caporali, 460 years before the name's 1912 record, so this is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not a pigment identification, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

issues: Fixed: the field-notes paragraph (and the matching "field" object) invented a painter claim ("Harald Foss's Fra Mariager Fjord, 1867") with no basis — ar.pa/ar.pn are empty for this slug — and the peak-decade stat (1860s/0.9%/6x) and the earliest-match painting+painter ("a 1568 Jacopo Bassano Adoration of the Magi") do not match any real field (real peak is the 1900s century fact, 0.5%/2.5x; real first-seen is a 1452 painting by Bartolomeo Caporali). The presence count (34) also didn't match either real count (31 within-painting / 58 as-photographed). Rewrote the paragraph directly from data/graph/fieldnotes for this slug; removed every unsupported claim rather than inventing a replacement for it.
